sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $4.86 billion to $14.3 billion [F1][F10][F198].
The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue jumped 89.1% in FY2021 to $16.1 billion, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12.2 billion [D241][F6][D292][F7].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of FY2021 growth at 36.3% of revenue, and its disappearance subtracted 36.3pp in FY2022 [D582][D580][D585].
Since then growth has slowed to 7.8%, 8.3% and 1.0% in FY2023 to FY2025, while operating margin fell 4 years running from 55.7% to 24.9% [D342][D391][D440][F26][F30][R1].
In FY2025 the growth engine flipped: net product sales fell 17.3% and subtracted 9.3pp, while collaboration revenue grew 21.0% and added 9.0pp [D506][D507][D522][D523].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4%, subtracting 14.2pp, on lower volumes from competitive pressure, compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition, plus a lower net selling price [D577][D578][P10].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% and contributed 9.3pp, driven by higher Dupixent sales [D591][D592][P9].
Operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 5.4%, so operating income fell 10.3% against revenue growth of 1.0% [D464][D457][D441][D440].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% against net income growth of 2.1% as the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D444][D442][D459].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 is the window low, below the 34.6% median and far below the 55.7% high of FY2021 [F30][D749][D751][D750].
The FY2025 bridge was R&D -4.7pp, SG&A +2.0pp and other lines -0.5pp, netting the 3.2pp decline [D465][D466][D467][D453].
R&D rose 14.0% to 40.8% of revenue, the highest share since FY2016, while SG&A fell 8.6% on lower charitable contributions to Good Days [D455][D420][D456][P5].
Net margin of 31.4% sat 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin, as other income of $1.65 billion and a 13.9% tax rate lifted the bottom line [F50][F30][X117][D427].
Operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income in FY2025, and free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x, below the 1.09x window high [F80][F40][D428][F100][D429][D762].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% sits above the 26.4% window median and the 22.0% peer median [D425][D757][D777].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898 million, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A, as the Tarrytown and Rensselaer build-out continued [D447][F90][D424][D430][P19].
Stock-based compensation of $994 million was 20.0% of operating cash flow, a persistent non-cash add-back [X77][D431].
Net cash of $16.9 billion equals 117.7% of revenue, in the 100th percentile of the eight-peer group against a -50.7% median [D434][D435][D780][D781].
Total debt is $1.99 billion against $18.9 billion of cash and investments, and the current ratio is 4.13x [D433][D432][F180].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.81 billion consumed 93.3% of free cash flow in FY2025, up from 71.0% in FY2024 [D436][D437][D388].
Return on average equity fell to 14.9%, in the 25th percentile against a 38.7% peer median [D439][D784][D785].
Operating margin has fallen four straight years, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].
The compression is structural rather than cyclical: EYLEA is shrinking and R&D intensity is rising, so the FY2021 peak is unlikely to recur [R1].
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table are later recasts, $5.15 billion and $6.56 billion against $6.71 billion and $7.86 billion first reported [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2018-FY2019 comparisons should not be read as reported [R2].
Whether US EYLEA sales stabilize above the FY2025 level of $2.75 billion, in the FY2026 10-K [S43].
Whether operating margin holds above the FY2025 window low of 24.9%, in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D749].
Whether R&D as a share of revenue falls back below the 40.8% FY2025 level, in the FY2026 10-K [D420].
